attempts.summary: Installed and configured zram-generator on node1 to provide compressed in-memory swap (zstd algorithm, ~981 MB, exceeding the 512 MB minimum) with swap-priority=100, which activates automatically at boot via /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf and systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service. No disk-backed swap exists, so zram is inherently preferred; its high priority (100) also ensures it would be preferred over any disk swap added later (disk swap defaults to priority -2). Verified via a full node restart: boot ID changed from 4a743885... to 91329670..., confirming a genuine reboot, and post-restart checks show zram0 swap active with the same size/algorithm/priority with no manual intervention.
